newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Juppe says euro to be growth tool.
newsitem.headline: France's Juppe says euro to be growth tool.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Tuesday that Europe and the single European currency would be an instrument of growth and stability.
"Europe will be an instrument of stability and therefore an instrument of growth," Juppe told a cheering audience at campaign rally.
"Those who say the euro equals rigour are telling stories," he said. "The creation of the euro should allow us to put in place a strategy of growth."
He also said that if Italy and Spain met all the requirements in the Maastricht treaty on monetary union, they should be allowed to particitpate in the euro from its launch on January 1, 1999.
"The objective is clear, there must be the greatest number of European countries as possible in the euro and if Italy and Spain fulfill the criteria, they must be included," he said.
Juppe blamed the opposition Socialists for France's high deficits and economic problems and said that even without the Maastricht treaty, France had to lower its deficits.
"Maastricht or not, we must absolutely stop the spiral of deficits" in France.
Juppe was campaigning for a snap, two-round parliamentary election called for May 25 and June 1.
